q: How many litres are there in a tonne of diesel in India?
title: Litres in a tonne of diesel
short: PPAC's conversion table gives 1,210 litres per tonne of diesel, measured at 29.5 C. To move that volume to the 15 C basis used on bulk invoices, multiply by 0.9879, which gives about 1,195 litres. That implies a density near 0.837 kg per litre at 15 C.
audience: Fleet owners, factories with DG sets, fuel buyers

ul: Weight to volume: 1 tonne of diesel = 1.2100 kilolitres = 7.61 barrels (PPAC Ready Reckoner FY 2025-26, Table 9.2).
Temperature: to convert volume at 29.5 C to volume at 15 C, multiply by 0.9879.
PPAC notes that petrol and diesel figures are as per BS-IV norms.

p: Use it when a supplier invoices diesel in tonnes or kilolitres and you need the other unit, or to sanity-check a quantity. If the invoice or test certificate prints a density, use that instead: it describes your actual batch.
Once you have kilograms, multiply by the IPCC default of about 3.19 kg CO2 per kg of diesel. Working in mass avoids most temperature and density errors.
